paragraphs.text: tts tool that turns text into an audio file through any OpenAI-compatible TTS backend.
# dsh-tts

Text-to-speech plugin for dsh: one `tts` tool that turns text into an audio
file (wav / mp3 / flac /

aac / opus / pcm) through any OpenAI-compatible TTS
backend, so agents can voice their output witho

ut per-backend glue. The same
tool lists voices and models, probes the routes, and calls the backend

's dev
phonemize endpoint.
## Tool verbs
| verb        | network | what it does |
| `synth`     | yes     | Synthesizes the requested speech. The tool writes the audio file to disk a

nd runs container checks on the returned bytes. |
| `voices`    | yes     | Lists the backend voices
, optionally filtered. When the backend returns 404 to `GET {baseURL}/audio/voices`, the tool serves

the static OpenAI table and marks `source: static`. |
| `providers` | no      | Lists the configure
d routes with their fields, the originating layer of each field, and the credential state. The verb

reads the local configuration and makes no network request. |
| `models`    | maybe   | Reports the
model list of each route. A route with declared models reports the declared list from the config lay

er, and a route without declared models reports the live `GET {baseURL}/models` probe. |
| `status`
| yes     | Probes each route: the `GET {baseURL}/models` listing plus the optional server-root `

GET /health` liveness probe. |
| `phonemize` | yes     | Calls the backend's `POST /dev/phonemize` e
ndpoint at the server root. A 404 or 405 response reports the endpoint as unsupported. |
Key `synth` behaviors:

- The `voice` argument is required, and there is no default: the voice set is
provider-specific. The

available ids are listed by the `voices` verb.
- When the call omits `model`, the tool uses the rou

te's single declared
model. When a route declares no models, the tool resolves the model by a
live `

/models` probe. When the declared or probed model list contains
several models, the call fails and l

ists the candidates.
- The `response_format` argument defaults to `wav`, and the tool sends the
valu

e verbatim.
- The backend owns container correctness, and the tool validates the returned
bytes: a R

IFF walk for `wav`, and magic checks for the other formats
(`pcm` carries no container check). When

the payload is not the claimed
container, the call fails and the tool keeps the file on disk. When t

he
container carries a known defect, for example the placeholder RIFF chunk
sizes (`0xFFFFFFFF` or `

0x7FFFFFFF`) some backends emit, the successful
document reports it in `warnings`.

Configuration is layered: built-in defaults, the `TTS_*` env contract, a
cordis patch file, a `dsh-t

ts` settings section (see below); the plugin
creates no config or state files.
## Configuration

Providers are configured in any of four layers, lowest to highest priority;
the `providers` verb rep

orts the originating layer of every field, so a
shadowed value is never silent:

1. the built-in default (`api: openai-compatible`),
2. the `TTS_*` env contract (static per process

boot),
3. the cordis config layer (a patch entry with id `dsh-tts` and a `config`
object, or profile

-level patches),
4. the `dsh-tts:` section in the user settings document
(`$DSH_HOME/settings.yaml`)

, which the plugin re-reads on every call, so
settings edits apply without a restart.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The env contract mirrors the config fields 1:1: `TTS_DEFAULT_PROVIDER`,
and per route `<NAME>` the v

ariables `TTS_PROVIDER_<NAME>_BASEURL`,
`TTS_PROVIDER_<NAME>_API`, `TTS_PROVIDER_<NAME>_APIKEYENV`,

`TTS_PROVIDER_<NAME>_HEADERS`, `TTS_PROVIDER_<NAME>_MODELS`,
`TTS_PROVIDER_<NAME>_DISPLAYNAME`. The

`<NAME>` segment is the route name
uppercased with `-` written as `_`. The `headers` value is a JSON

object
string, and the `models` value is a comma-separated list of model ids. The
`baseURL` value i

s the OpenAI-compatible base URL including the `/v1` prefix
(the same shape as an LLM provider base

URL); the plugin appends
`/audio/speech`, `/audio/voices`, and `/models` to it verbatim, and it
addr

esses `/health` and `/dev/phonemize` at the server root, which it derives
by stripping a trailing `/

v1` from the base URL. The `apiKeyEnv` value is a
reference to an environment variable name, never a

secret in config; per
request the value resolves from the process environment, then from
`$DSH_HOME
/.credentials.yaml`.

## Troubleshooting

A failing call returns a JSON document with an `error` message field, and the
message text identifie

returns a JSON document with an `error` message field, and the
message text identifies the failure.

- When the error message is "TTS_NOT_CONFIGURED", no route survived
configuration. Check the base UR

Ls; the tool reports each route that
configuration drops as a warning in the log.
- When the error m

essage carries the text "credential missing: environment
variable "X" is not set", the credential re

ference does not resolve. Set
`X` in the environment or add it to `$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml`.
- W

hen the error message carries the text "unknown provider "x"", the route
name matches no configured

route. Route names match case-insensitively and
treat `_` and `-` as the same separator; the error l

ists the configured
names.
- When the error message carries the text "multiple providers configured

(...) and no default is set", pass the `provider` argument explicitly, or
set `TTS_DEFAULT_PROVIDER`

, or set the settings `defaultProvider`.
- When `status` reports `reachable: false`, the `error` fie

ld carries the
cause; the probe uses a 15 s budget against `GET {baseURL}/models`.
- When `voices` r

eports `source: static`, the backend answered 404 to
`GET {baseURL}/audio/voices`, and the tool retu

rned the static OpenAI
table. The listed voice ids may not exist on that backend.
- When the synth d

ocument carries a container check error, the tool could not
verify the returned bytes as the claimed

container. Inspect the kept file
at `out`; the backend may return an unsupported container for the

requested
`response_format`.
